extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers of philosophy (metaphysics/epistemology) interested in Bergson's theory of negation, nothing, and duration
extracted.subtask_description: Close philosophical exposition of the concepts of Nothing, negation, and duration; examines how ideas of absence/non-existence are formed and why conceiving an absolute annihilation is self-contradictory. Advises on proper method for thinking being and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coexistence criterion for a legitimate idea
rubrics_metrics.description: An idea constructed by the mind is an idea only if its pieces are capable of coexisting; it is reduced to a mere word if the elements that we bring together to compose it are driven away as fast as we assemble them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by the impossibility of a 'square circle' and by the contrast with representable objects (black circle, white circle, circle in cardboard). If components cannot coherently coexist under the concept, the purported idea is empty verbalism rather than genuine thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation is not symmetrical with affirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Negation is but the half of an intellectual act and differs from affirmation: it is an affirmation of the second degree (a judgment on a judgment) and involves a non-intellectual element (social/pedagogical intent and feeling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat negation as producing ideas sui generis equal and opposite to affirmations. When one denies, one implicitly refers to a possible affirmation and to a (often unspecified) substitution; negation functions to warn or correct rather than to supply positive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-existence must be represented by positing exclusion/substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: To represent an object as 'non-existent' cannot consist in simply withdrawing the idea of existence; it consists in adding the idea of an exclusion of this particular object by actual reality in general (i.e., positing that some other reality supplants it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thinking 'A is not' already presupposes the idea of A (and thus of A's existence as possible) plus an implicit replacement or exclusion. One cannot represent pure non-existence without implicitly representing the real that excludes it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of absence is composite: substitution + feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The representation of the void (absence) always resolves into two positive elements: the idea (distinct or confused) of a substitution, and the feeling, experienced or imagined, of a desire or a regret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing claims of absence or annihilation, look for these two constituent parts. The 'nothing' we speak of is psychologically constituted by an imagined substitution together with an affective tinge (preference, disappointment), not by a pure empty content.

rubrics_metrics.name: The idea of annihilation of everything is self-contradictory (pseudo-idea)
rubrics_metrics.description: If suppressing a thing consists in replacing it by another, the suppression of absolutely everything implies a contradiction in terms; the 'annihilation of everything' is as absurd as a square circle and thereby a mere word rather than a genuine idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware of constructing philosophical arguments that rely on imagining the annihilation of all things as a coherent notion. The method of successive negations (deny one thing after another) ignores that each negation implicitly invokes a substitute and so cannot reach a total annihilation coherently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid thinking being by detour through the concept of Nothing
rubrics_metrics.description: We must accustom ourselves to think being directly, without first passing through the phantom of the nought; otherwise the being we arrive at tends to be a static, mathematical essence rather than a psychological, temporal reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical method should aim for direct intuition/possession of being and duration ('install ourselves within it straight away') rather than reconstructing being via negation or abstract subtraction, which yields an atemporal, static conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation has a pedagogical/social function (practical orientation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Negation is addressed to a person (real or imagined) and serves to warn, correct, or guard against an error; it presupposes an interlocutor and therefore has a social and practical character rather than pure objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret negative propositions as interventions in social/pedagogical contexts (judgments on judgments). In philosophical analysis, distinguish this pragmatic function from claims about objective reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellect abstracts ends (points of rest) and thereby risks static conceptions of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The function of the intellect is to preside over actions by representing ends (results) explicitly while letting the movements constituting the action elude consciousness; it pictures points of rest rather than continuous movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing actions or duration, do not conflate the intellect's tendency to focus on end-states with the full temporal continuity of lived duration. To grasp duration, 'install yourself within it' rather than abstracting only final states.
